What is a multi-stage build?: A multi-stage build uses multiple FROM instructions to build artifacts in one stage and then copy only the required runtime files into a smaller final stage. This keeps the final image lean and avoids shipping build-time dependencies.
What is the difference between ADD and C: COPY simply copies local files and directories into the image. ADD also supports fetching remote URLs and automatic extraction of local tar archives, which makes it less predictable and often unnecessary.

What is Terraform State?: Terraform state is the metadata file that records the current mapping between configuration and real infrastructure resources, including resource IDs, attributes, and dependency graph information.
What happens if the Terraform state file: Terraform loses track of managed resources. You must restore from backup or re-import resources, otherwise Terraform may try to recreate existing resources incorrectly.
How do you import existing resources int: Define the matching resource block in configuration and run terraform import <resource_address> <resource_id>. Then reconcile the imported resource with the config by running plan and adjusting the configuration as needed.
Does terraform import generate the compl: No. terraform import updates state only. You still need to write the full configuration and variable definitions yourself.
What happens if someone manually changes: Terraform detects drift on the next plan and can show changes. If applied, it may restore the resource to match configuration or require manual reconciliation.
Explain your Terraform folder/module str: I use a root module per environment or service, shared reusable modules under modules/, separate state backends per environment, and clear inputs/outputs. I keep environment-specific values in tfvars and use module boundaries to encapsulate reusable infrastructure patterns.
Why shouldn’t the Terraform state file b: Local state is not shared, has no locking, and can be lost or corrupted. Remote state backends provide collaboration, locking, backups, and access control.
If two engineers run terraform apply sim: A properly configured remote backend will lock the state and serialize the operations. If locking is unavailable, simultaneous applies can corrupt the state and cause conflicting infrastructure changes.
How do you remove a stale Terraform stat: Use terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID> after verifying that no active terraform process is still holding the lock.

Explain Readiness Probe, Liveness Probe,: Readiness probes determine when a pod can receive traffic. Liveness probes check whether the container is still healthy and restart it if it has failed. What happens when a Readiness Probe fail: The pod is removed from the service endpoints and no longer receives new traffic until it becomes ready again.

What causes a CrashLoopBackOff?: A CrashLoopBackOff occurs when a container repeatedly fails and restarts, often due to an application error, bad command, missing dependency, bad configuration, or probe failure.

What is Linux Load Average?: Load average is the average number of runnable processes and uninterruptible I/O tasks over a period of time.
At what load average does it become crit: It becomes critical when the load average consistently exceeds the number of CPU cores, especially by a large factor, because it indicates more work is waiting than can be executed.
What is the difference between Free Memo: Free memory is the amount of RAM not used at all. Available memory includes free memory plus reclaimable cache and buffers that can be used without swapping.
What is Swap Memory?: Swap memory is disk-backed virtual memory used when physical RAM is insufficient, allowing the system to keep inactive pages in swap space.
If the disk usage reaches 95%, what woul: I would identify large files, rotate and archive logs, remove temporary or stale data, clean package caches, and free space safely while preserving critical data.

CPU usage suddenly spikes, but no proces: It could be system-level activity like interrupts, I/O wait, kernel work, blocked processes, stolen CPU from virtualization, or a process that is only briefly consuming CPU between measurement intervals.
